title: Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement - District and Trustees of the California State University, on behalf of California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt - Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement (MOU or Agreement) for an Intern Partnership Program and Practica Program applying to credentials in TK-12 Teaching, including Multiple Subjects, Single Subjects, Designated Subjects, and Special Education Categories, including Added or Supplementary Authorizations; including Pupil Personnel Services in Communicative Sciences & Disorders, Mental Health & Wellness, Counseling & Guidance, Education Intervention or Educational Therapy, Social Work, Administration, and other Pupil Personnel Services credentials and certifications, as may be specified; including Fieldwork Experience for Master of Arts or Science and other Graduate-Level Degrees or Certifications with Emphasis in Pupil Personnel Services; including Fieldwork Experience for Pre-Credential Candidate Undergraduate Students-is entered into by and between Oakland Unified School District (District or OUSD), a public school district in the State of California, County of Alameda, and the Trustees of California State University, on behalf of the California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt (University or CSPUH), a California State University-for the term July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031 at no cost to the District other than for certain Non-Teaching Interns in PPS categories (Article 6/#6), who are not employees of the District but may be allocated stipends (Article 6/#6) drawn from non-profit organizational grants to the District (e.g. Ed Fund), administered by the relevant departments of the District. [See Fiscal Impact]
headline: Five-year, no-cost partnership with Cal Poly Humboldt to host teacher and student-support interns

It runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031. It costs the district nothing, except that some non-teaching interns in student-support fields may receive stipends paid from nonprofit grants to the district, such as from the Ed Fund.
vendor_name: Trustees of the California State University, on behalf of California State Polytechnic University, Humboldt
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

headline: Hires a speech-language pathologist for up to $114,000 to serve students in special education
summary: Rachel Hart of San Leandro will work as a school-based speech and language pathologist for students with Individualized Education Programs (IEPs, their legal special education plans). Her duties include speech and language services, assessments, IEP meetings, progress reports, Medi-Cal billing, case management and communication with families and staff. The contract runs July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027 and is capped at $114,000.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Service Agreement 2025-2026 - Jacobson Education Law - Special Education Department

title: Service Agreement - Michelle Falise - Special Education Department

(CA License No. OC36861), covering All Enrolled Students While:

• On school campus grounds during regular school days and hours, including, whilst continuously on campus grounds, the hour immediately before and after scheduled classes.

• Participating in school-affiliated and supervised activities, including interscholastic athletics (excluding tackle football), off-season athletic training and conditioning, approved/sponsored work study, junior military programs, and field trip programs within the United States that remain under the control of school staff and/or designated adult chaperones.

headline: Pays Alliant Insurance $72,707.65 for 2026-27 accident insurance covering all enrolled students
summary: This insurance covers accidental injuries to all enrolled students while on campus during school hours, during supervised school activities such as sports (except tackle football) and field trips, and while traveling directly between home and school. title: Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement - Smith College - Talent/Human Resources Department
official_text: Approval by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding and Interagency Agreement (MOU or Agreement) for a Practicum Learning Experience Program-applying to District placements of College students, regarding course work for Advanced Degrees and Certifications, including the field of Social Work, and including Master of Arts or Science and other Graduate-Level Degrees or Certifications with Emphasis in Pupil Personnel Services, and other Pupil Personnel Services (PPS) credentials and certifications, as may be specified-is entered into by and between OAKLAND UNIFIED SCHOOL DISTRICT (District or OUSD), a public school district in the state of California, County of Alameda, and Smith College (SC or College), on behalf of its School For Social Work (SCSSW), an independent, nonprofit private college in Northampton, Massachusetts-for the term July 1, 2026 through June 30, 2031, at no cost to the District, other than for certain Non-Teaching Interns in PPS categories (Article 4/#2), who are not employees of the District but may be allocated stipends (Article 4/#3) drawn from non-profit organizational grants to the District (e.g. Ed Fund), administered by the relevant departments of the District. title: No Cost Services Agreement and Data Sharing Agreement - Board of Trustees of Stanford University - Stanford Graduate School of Education - Research, Assessment, and Data (RAD) Department
official_text: Ratification by the Board of Education of a No Cost Services Agreement (NCSA) and a Data Sharing Agreement (DSA), both, by and between the District and the Board of Trustees of Stanford University, on behalf f its Stanford Graduate School of Education, Stanford, CA, for the latter, under the NCSA, to partner with OUSD teachers to provide support for teachers' own goals though co-planning sessions and grow of their practice through thought partnership w/ researchers and other participants; provide OUSD with aggregated and de-identified information about multilingual learner math language practices which will be integrated into classrooms based on the participating teachers' goals; and facilitate OUSD to gain access to open-source tools built on the project to assess student math talk, for the period of January 30, 2026 through December 31, 2026, and under the DSA defining the terms and conditions of the District's transmission of or sharing of pupil data with the Board of Trustees of Stanford University, or its agent, and the protection by the Board of Trustees of Stanford University, or its agent, of such data, pursuant to the terms and conditions stated in the DSA, via, the Department of Secondary Instruction and the Research and Assessment Department (RAD), for the same term as specified in the NCSA, each Agreement, at no cost to the District.
headline: Ratifies a no-cost research partnership with Stanford to support teachers' math language practices
summary: The board is approving a no-cost services agreement with Stanford Graduate School of Education. Researchers will work with OUSD teachers on co-planning to support multilingual learners' math talk, share de-identified results and offer open-source tools. A data sharing agreement (DSA) sets rules for sharing and protecting student data. Both run January 30 through December 31, 2026, at no cost to the district.
vendor_name: Board of Trustees of Stanford University (Stanford Graduate School of Education)
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

title: Memorandum of Understanding - Alameda Health System - Community Schools and Student Services Department
official_text:
Ratification by the Board of Education of a Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) by and between the District and Alameda Health System (AHS), to help meet the medical health, mental health education and youth development needs of students, and through partnering with other services providers on campuses to provide a holistic set of wrap-around services that remove barriers to learning and ensure increase access to care, through school-based health centers, the latter will provide the following services: 
1. 	Dental screening and treatment
2. 	Health education for students and families
3. 	Outreach to youth and their families
4. 	Community-wide health promotion events and activities
5. 	Student referrals for services (at Frick Academy Wellness Center and alternate community clinics or community programs)
at no cost to the District, students, or parents unless provided otherwise by this MOU, for the period August 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027, via the Community Schools and Student Services Department.
headline: Ratifies a no-cost agreement with Alameda Health System for school-based health services
summary: This memorandum of understanding (MOU) has Alameda Health System offer services through school-based health centers: dental screening and treatment, health education for students and families, outreach, community health events, and referrals for care. The services are at no cost to the district, students or parents unless the MOU says otherwise. It covers August 1, 2026 through June 30, 2027.
outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report

summary: Children Rising will provide a coordinator to enroll families in its math and reading tutoring, update parents on their child's progress, and host monthly Zoom coaching sessions on learning strategies for home. outcome_action: Adopted on the General Consent Report
